extracted.intended_audience: Penn State assistant professors (early-career biomedical researchers) and research administrators preparing an institutional nomination for the Pew Biomedical Scholars program
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare an institutional nomination and application for the Pew Biomedical Scholars program (early-career research award for assistant professors running independent labs), following eligibility, selection, and internal limited-submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program focus / candidate promise
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pew Scholars Program in the Biomedical Sciences provides funding to young investigators of outstanding promise in science relevant to the advancement of human health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on performance during education and training, candidates should demonstrate outstanding promise as contributors in science relevant to human health.

rubrics_metrics.name: No clinical trials research
rubrics_metrics.description: This program does not fund clinical trials research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for creative, pioneering approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong proposals will incorporate particularly creative and pioneering approaches to basic, translational, and applied biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates whose work is based on biomedical principles but who bring in concepts and theories from more diverse fields are encouraged to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-impact potential encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas with the potential to produce an unusually high impact are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection factors: project description, evaluations, and past accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of the successful candidates will be based on a detailed description of the work that the applicant proposes to undertake, evaluations of the candidate’s performance, and notable past accomplishments, including honors, awards, and publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight on both project and researcher; evidence of independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Advisory Committee gives considerable weight to both the project proposal and the researcher, including evidence that the candidate is a successful independent investigator and has the skill set needed to carry out their high-impact proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for high-risk work unsuitable for NIH/NSF
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pew Charitable Trust is interested in funding projects that are not suitable for NIH or NSF funding due to high-risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding from the NIH, other government sources, and project grants from non-profit associations do not pose a conflict with the Pew scholars program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold a doctorate in biomedical sciences, medicine or a related field, including engineering or the physical sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and lab leadership requirement (as of specific date)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of Sept. 5, 2025, run an independent lab and hold a full-time appointment at the rank of assistant professor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible appointment types
rubrics_metrics.description: Current appointments such as research assistant professor, adjunct assistant professor, assistant professor research track, visiting professor, or instructor are not eligible to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four‑year appointment limit (appointment start cutoff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Must not have been appointed as an assistant professor and run an independent lab at any institution prior to June 11, 2021, whether or not such an appointment was on a tenure track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time spent in clinical internships, residencies, in work toward board certification, or on parental leave does not count as part of this four-year limit. Candidates who need an exception on the four-year limit should contact Pew’s program office to ensure that application reviewers are aware an exception has been given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary COVID-related eligibility extension note
rubrics_metrics.description: The eligibility criteria above have been temporarily expanded to account for COVID-related lab shutdowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extension will end after this upcoming application cycle. Beginning next year, the eligibility window for the 2027 grant will revert to the three-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application frequency limit
rubrics_metrics.description: May apply to the program a maximum of two times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination by institution required; application completion
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants must be nominated by their institution and must complete the 2026 online application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on changing nominating institution
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicants have appointments at more than one eligible nominating institution or affiliate, they may not reapply in a subsequent year from a different nominating entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual exclusivity with Pew-Stewart program
rubrics_metrics.description: May not be nominated for the Pew Scholars Program and the Pew-Stewart Scholars Program for Cancer Research in the same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional limited-submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2026 award, one nomination will be invited from each of the participating institutions listed at the bottom of this page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission Limit per Institution: 1; Available Tickets: 1. Questions concerning the limited submissions process may be submitted to limitedsubs@psu.edu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key internal and sponsor dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal and sponsor deadlines must be met as part of the limited submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal deadline (updated): April 14, 2025 at 4:00 p.m.; Sponsor internal nomination due: May 14, 2025; Pew application due: September 3, 2025. (Sponsor deadline listed as May 14, 2025 elsewhere on the page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative advisory: review sponsor guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully review the program guidelines and the sponsor's website for any requirements and expectations related to eligibility, PI and Co-PI limits, budget, collaboration, priority research areas, letter of intent requirements, and review criteria before submitting to this internal competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and period
rubrics_metrics.description: The current grant level is $300,000; $75,000 per year for a four-year period.
